scope: One read-only contract check of the fixed 89 TRAIN and 2233 TEST financial records, current raw Parquet id/question_text/options/answer projection on NEW, and nine proof-bound OLD prediction metadata files for the fixed three methods at S0/S16/S19.
findings: Raw source comparisons preserve the original string/list answer construction and distinguish question, context, metadata options, selected answer and all references. Non-choice/unparseable input is not automatically treated as an error.
The strict input-only option parser matches the old parser. It is not used to parse generated answers or replace original scoring.

All parsed option contents and complete original label-plus-content spans are now checked against retained context; failed verbatim retention is an investigation signal, not automatic proof of semantic loss.

Original methods and proof hashes are pinned. OLD historical runner source SHA and input_batch AST are checked; OLD config SHA/method/backbone/manifest are validated there and returned rather than assuming old run configs exist on NEW.
SSH invocation correctly replaces python -c script with python - and sends a script embedding the JSON bundle through stdin; fixed data/code do not depend on shell escaping of a large -c argument.

Missing saved retrieval records, absent actual TRAIN prompt records and lack of historical full tokenized-input equality are explicit. Zero anomalies cannot be interpreted as complete input fidelity when evidence is missing.
Public output contains counts and hashes only; anomaly IDs/reasons are private. No generated answer text, old score calculation, 129-certificate recomputation or model request is included.
limitations: The current raw four-column projection is an independent field comparison, not a newly verified historical whole-Parquet SHA chain.
Author label agreement and presence of a corresponding option do not establish semantic correctness of that gold answer.
Input-source reconstruction and saved retrieval indexes do not prove old tokenizer/chat-template input equality; no actual processor call is permitted.
TRAIN/TEST answer distributions are descriptive and cannot prove why a model chose A or B or justify TEST-based prompt, label, route, loss or sampling changes.
The 180-second independent supervision is an execution requirement outside the reviewed consumer. The consumer itself uses a 120-second alarm and 75-second SSH subprocess timeout.
No data consumer, SSH, raw Parquet reader, model, tensor, processor, QA generation, training, score or bootstrap was executed in this review.
